head: ScreenRecess screen time app for iPhone pauses a group of apps
dek: ScreenRecess is a new $4.99 iPhone and iPad app that gives a group of apps one shared time allowance, then locks them for a break. It was #62 in Productivity among paid apps on the US App Store on 15 November.
details: You pick the apps, set an allowance of 1 to 60 minutes and a break of 15 to 60 minutes, or use presets such as 10 minutes on, 15 off. You can also start a break early. The listing says it counts use in whole minutes, so a block can start a little late, and there's no countdown timer. It's a one-time purchase with no subscription, needs iOS 26 and Screen Time permission, and its maker Abdulazeez Otori says it collects no data.
where: iPhone and iPad, App Store, $4.99 one-time
means: If Apple's own app limits are too easy to wave away, this puts several apps on one shared clock and forces a pause.
todo: Start with one of the presets for a few days before setting your own numbers.
thumb_words: ONE TIME LIMIT FOR ALL YOUR APPS
